consensus_summary: Israel primarily signifies God’s covenant people, most commonly extended symbolically to the Church as true/spiritual Israel (Jew and Gentile in Christ), while major alternatives retain ethnic/national Israel as distinct or treat Christ as true Israel; no single settled extension.
book_summary: The covenant name given to Jacob and borne at several scales—the man, his descendants, the nation, or the faithful people who prevail with God—with sense fixed by context, not blood alone.
consensus_core_identification: God’s covenant people (commonly the Church as spiritual Israel)
book_core_identification: Covenant name of Jacob applied polyvalently (man/descendants/nation/faithful prevailers) by context, not blood
boundary_disagreement: Book explicitly admits individual Jacob, ethnic descendants, nation, and faithful remnant as co-equal contextual senses and denies blood as decisive; consensus typically privileges the corporate people/Church debate and treats the personal or purely national senses as background rather than definitional scales.
rationale: Minimum cores both identify Israel as the covenant identity originating in Jacob’s renaming and not settled by physical descent alone (Gen 32:28; Rom 9:6). The book preserves that category while broadening and re-precisioning the admitted cases to multiple simultaneous scales determined by context; this is a boundary refinement, not a replacement of the central referent.
strongest_objection: Consensus primaries frequently foreground the Church-as-Israel reading, which the book entry neither names nor excludes.
